title: Chapter 10 - Simple API Examples (GET and POST)
description: Quick concept check on basic API calls.

questions.prompt: In a GET request, you usually:

options.label: Send new data to create a resource

explanations.overview: GET is used to read data.

byOptionId.b: Not quite. Creating is usually POST.
byOptionId.c: Not quite. Delete is for DELETE.
byOptionId.d: Not quite. Update is PATCH or PUT.

questions.prompt: Why do you add a JSON body in a POST request?

options.label: To send the data you want to create

explanations.overview: POST bodies carry the data to create or process.

byOptionId.a: Correct. The body sends new data.
byOptionId.b: Not quite. The URL is separate.
byOptionId.c: Not quite. Status codes are always returned.

questions.prompt: What does the Content-Type header tell the server?

options.label: The format of the data you send

explanations.overview: Content-Type tells the server the data format, like JSON.

byOptionId.a: Correct. It describes the data format.
byOptionId.b: Not quite. Screen size is unrelated.
byOptionId.c: Not quite. Keyboard layout is unrelated.
byOptionId.d: Not quite. Wi-Fi name is unrelated.

explanations.overview: fetch() sends HTTP requests from the browser.

byOptionId.b: Not quite. It does not create databases.
byOptionId.d: Not quite. Formatting drives is unrelated.
